high.title: Bursa ends at intraday high, led by financial and healthcare sectors
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 6.93 points to close at 1,732.66, buoyed by a rebound in US technology stocks and renewed confidence in the AI theme. Investors remained selective amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia, favouring sectors with resilient earnings and strong domestic fundamentals. This closing performance is significant for Malaysian investors tracking overall market direction and sector allocation.

high.title: Ringgit eases against greenback, higher against other currencies
high.summary: The ringgit slipped marginally against the US dollar to 4.0945/4.0985 at 6pm, as upbeat US economic data pushed the DXY above the 100-point mark, reinforcing USD strength. Bank Muamalat's chief economist noted the ringgit was largely flat against the dollar but gained against a basket of other major currencies. This currency movement is critical for Malaysian businesses with USD-denominated trade and investors monitoring forex risk.

high.title: Ringgit falls against US dollar, major currencies as Treasury yields rise
high.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.0935/4.0975 against the US dollar, driven by rising US Treasury yields and a stronger Japanese yen following likely Bank of Japan intervention. Key US labour market data including nonfarm payrolls on August 7 will be critical in determining the dollar's near-term direction, posing significant implications for the ringgit's trajectory.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar ahead of key US economic data
high.summary: The ringgit opened stronger after Trump cancelled planned military strikes on Iran, easing geopolitical risk and weakening the US dollar. However, caution remains as rising Brent crude prices and upcoming US ISM Manufacturing PMI data could influence currency movements, with the ringgit expected to trade in a narrow RM4.07–RM4.09 range.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on blue-chip buying, tracks regional markets
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 4.50 points at 1,724.90, supported by foreign buying returning to the local market. Regional sentiment was broadly positive, with South Korea's KOSPI surging 17.91% and Japan's Nikkei rising 4.03%, while the Bank of Japan held rates steady as expected. The return of foreign capital inflows is a key positive signal for Malaysian equity markets.

high.title: Ringgit ends week higher as weak US data weighs on dollar
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0835/4.0875 against the US dollar, boosted by weaker-than-expected US Q2 GDP growth of 1.5% versus a 2.1% consensus forecast. The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE index, also moderated to 3.7% in June, softening the dollar. Despite this, expectations of a September Fed rate hike remain intact, which could limit further ringgit gains.

high.title: Bursa's key index ends at an intraday high on continued buying support
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed higher driven by rotation into consumer and plantation stocks despite weaker Wall Street sentiment, diverging from regional peers. The US Fed held rates steady for the fifth consecutive meeting at 3.50%-3.75%, while renewed US-Iran hostilities pushed crude oil prices higher. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia continue to cloud the near-term outlook and could elevate volatility across regional equities.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher as US Fed holds rate steady
high.summary: The ringgit edged higher against the US dollar following the Fed's decision to hold the Federal Funds Rate at 3.50%-3.75%, which caused the US dollar index to fall 0.57%. The decision was not unanimous, with 3 of 12 voting members favouring a rate hike, signalling lingering hawkish sentiment. The US Treasury yield curve steepened, with the 10-year yield rising 7 basis points to 4.68%, indicating tighter financial conditions ahead.

high.title: Ringgit closes marginally higher ahead of FOMC outcome
high.summary: The ringgit held steady in a range-bound session as markets awaited the FOMC decision, with the potential for a hawkish tone to boost the US dollar. West Asia tensions escalated as US forces intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles, sending WTI and Brent crude oil prices surging by over 3.6%. Rising crude oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty are key factors influencing both the ringgit and broader Malaysian market sentiment.

medium.title: Bursa retreats after early gains amid cautious sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI dipped 2.58 points to 1,723.15 in early morning trade despite opening higher, reflecting cautious investor sentiment. Market breadth remained positive with gainers outpacing losers, and Wall Street's strong Monday performance on easing US-Iran tensions provided some support. This intraday update offers context for Malaysian investors on opening market dynamics and external drivers.

medium.title: Ringgit opens flat against dollar after upbeat US factory data
medium.summary: The ringgit opened little changed at 4.0935/4.1000 against the USD as stronger-than-expected US ISM Manufacturing PMI data reinforced expectations of a US interest rate hike. The DXY held near the 100-point level while declining crude oil prices, driven by US-Iran negotiation optimism, added a mixed backdrop. Malaysian businesses and investors should monitor these developments given their implications for import costs and monetary policy divergence.

medium.title: Maybank said to be near buying Ageas stake in Etiqa
medium.summary: Maybank is reportedly close to acquiring Ageas's 31% stake in Etiqa Insurance for approximately US$1.2 billion, valuing the entire insurer at roughly US$4 billion. This would consolidate Maybank's full ownership of Etiqa, significantly strengthening its insurance arm and potentially impacting Maybank's capital allocation and earnings outlook.

medium.title: Bursa ends slightly higher on late buying in selected heavyweights
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed marginally higher as late bargain hunting offset broader regional weakness tied to AI spending concerns and tech valuation worries. Easing geopolitical tensions following Trump's signal on Strait of Hormuz negotiations caused Brent crude to fall sharply, supporting sentiment, with the FBM KLCI expected to trade in the 1,710–1,740 range this week.

medium.title: Bursa retreats on cautious sentiment and profit taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 4.56 points to 1,720.34 in early trade as profit-taking and cautious sentiment weighed on the market despite last week's gains supported by Wall Street's positive performance. Market breadth was negative with losers outpacing gainers, reflecting investor wariness amid uncertain global economic conditions.

medium.title: Ringgit opens higher as weaker US data weighs on dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0800/4.0885 against the greenback as the US Dollar Index fell 1.01% following softer US economic data. US Q2 GDP came in at 1.5% and PCE inflation eased to 3.7%, supporting the Fed's decision to hold rates near-term. This opening strength set a positive tone for Malaysian currency markets heading into the trading day.

medium.title: Ringgit ends mostly higher regionally, flat against US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit was flat against the US dollar at 4.0875/4.0930 following the FOMC decision to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, though three of 12 voting members favoured a rate hike. The split decision signals a possible rate increase at the September FOMC meeting, which could strengthen the US dollar and pressure the ringgit. Malaysian investors should monitor Fed communication closely ahead of the September 15-16 meeting.

medium.title: Bursa opens mixed amid Wall Street gains, geopolitical concerns
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 2.04 points at the open despite Wall Street gains, as geopolitical tensions weighed on sentiment following a drone strike on gas vessels at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta. The widening US-Iran conflict introduces energy supply risks that could impact oil prices and Malaysian energy-linked stocks. Market breadth remained positive with gainers outnumbering losers.

medium.title: Bursa edges down as investors digest Fed decision
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 2.68 points to 1,712.88 in early trade as investors digested the Fed's rate hold decision and weighed the impact of US strikes on Iran following an attack on a US military base in Jordan. The broader market was negative with losers outpacing gainers significantly, reflecting cautious sentiment. Trading volume was thin at 98.08 million shares worth RM56.55 million in the early session.

medium.title: Defensive stocks lift Bursa at close
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.08 points to 1,715.56, supported by consumer products, services, and telecommunications stocks which provided a defensive buffer against geopolitical headwinds. Reports of Iranian missile strikes on US military facilities renewed Middle East conflict concerns and brought energy security back into investor focus. Turnover remained healthy at 2.96 billion units valued at RM2.48 billion, with gainers outpacing decliners.
